title: Kernel geometry and homology of a fixed successive lower truncation transition
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], $K$ a cochain complex, and $m\in\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $q:\tau_{\ge m}K\to\tau_{\ge m+1}K$ satisfy $\pi_m q=\pi_{m+1}$, where canonical lower truncation is zero below the cutoff, opcycles at the cutoff, and $K$ above. Write $B=\ker q$. There is a morphism $\varphi:H^m(K)[-m]\to B$ and isomorphisms $e_0:B^m\simeq K^m/\operatorname{im}d^{m-1}$ and $e_1:B^{m+1}\simeq\operatorname{im}d^m$. Under these isomorphisms the kernel inclusion is the identity at $m$ and the image inclusion at $m+1$, the differential is induced by $d^m$, and $\varphi^m$ is the canonical homology inclusion into opcycles. All other terms of $B$ vanish, and $\varphi$ is a quasi-isomorphism. These conditions determine $\varphi$ uniquely.

proof.text: For an abelian category $\mathcal A$, a cochain complex $K$, and $m\in\mathbf Z$, assume $q:\tau_{\ge m}K\to\tau_{\ge m+1}K$ satisfies $\pi_m q=\pi_{m+1}$. The canonical projection is degreewise epi, so this identity uniquely determines every component of $q$. At $m$ the target is zero; at $m+1$ the first projection is invertible and the second is the opcycles quotient. Above $m+1$ both projections are invertible. Evaluation preserves kernels, so its kernel in degree $m$ is opcycles, in degree $m+1$ is the image of $d^m$, and is zero elsewhere. The resulting isomorphisms are characterized by their composites with the kernel inclusion. Below $m$ the source vanishes, and in higher degrees the kernel of an isomorphism vanishes.

proof.text: The chain map identity for the kernel inclusion gives $\iota^m d_C=d_{\tau}^m\iota^{m+1}$. Substitute the two kernel isomorphisms and the truncation differential formula. Cancellation of the image inclusion yields the differential from $K^m/\operatorname{im}d^{m-1}$ onto $\operatorname{im}d^m$. Its composite with the image inclusion is precisely the map induced by $d^m$, giving the displayed differential equality.

proof.text: The homology inclusion $H^m(K)\to K^m/\operatorname{im}d^{m-1}$ lies in the kernel of this induced differential. Transport it by the degree-$m$ isomorphism and construct a chain map from the single complex: all its other components are zero. The differential condition is the vanishing just stated. The component formula and the monic kernel inclusion determine this chain map uniquely, including in the zero and acyclic cases.

proof.text: Since the kernel has no term before $m$, its degree-$m$ cohomology is the kernel of the induced differential, namely $H^m(K)$, and the single-complex map induces the identity. The induced differential onto the image is epi, so degree-$m+1$ cohomology is zero. All remaining cohomology groups vanish because the corresponding terms are zero. The single complex has cohomology only in degree $m$, so all homology maps are invertible, which is the quasi-isomorphism condition.

theorem exists_lowerTruncationTransitionKernel
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C]
    (K : CochainComplex C ℤ) (m : ℤ)
    (q : K.truncGE m ⟶ K.truncGE (m + 1))
    (hq : K.πTruncGE m ≫ q = K.πTruncGE (m + 1)) :
    ∃ (φ : ((singleFunctor C m).obj (K.homology m)) ⟶ kernel q),
      (∃ (e₀ : (kernel q).X m ≅ K.opcycles m)
            (e₁ : (kernel q).X (m + 1) ≅
              Abelian.image (K.d m (m + 1))),
            e₀.inv ≫ (kernel.ι q).f m =
              (K.truncGEXIsoOpcycles m).inv ∧
            e₁.inv ≫ (kernel.ι q).f (m + 1) ≫
              (K.truncGEXIso m (m + 1)).hom =
                Abelian.image.ι (K.d m (m + 1)) ∧
            e₀.inv ≫ (kernel q).d m (m + 1) ≫ e₁.hom ≫
              Abelian.image.ι (K.d m (m + 1)) =
                K.fromOpcycles m (m + 1) ∧
            (HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (ComplexShape.up ℤ) m
                (K.homology m)).inv ≫ φ.f m ≫ e₀.hom =
                  K.homologyι m) ∧
      (∀ (r : ℤ), r ≠ m → r ≠ m + 1 → IsZero ((kernel q).X r)) ∧
      QuasiIso φ
